qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: High customer switching costs driven by installed base of testing instruments requiring proprietary chemical reagents and testing kits. Testing represents <1% of customer operating budget but is legally mandated for municipal water compliance and product traceability, granting sustained 2-3% annual pricing power over inflation. Proven by 27% median GAAP ROIC and ~60% gross margins.
qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates. Essential water quality analytics and packaging coding oligopoly with 60%+ recurring revenue from proprietary consumables. Moat protected by extreme switching costs, regulatory mandates (EPA/Clean Water Act), and Danaher Business System operational DNA (VES). Pristine balance sheet with net cash position and >95% FCF conversion. [5-10Y g: water & packaging volume 3.5% + proprietary consumable price 2.0% + bolt-on M&A reinvestment 1.5% + net share buybacks 1.0% - tariff/tax drags 0.5%]
qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle capital efficiency demonstrated by 27.1% 5-year median GAAP ROIC, tangible operating ROIC >100%, and consistent 58-60% gross margins. Water Quality (~60% of revenue; Hach, Trojan, ChemTreat) provides essential water testing instruments and proprietary reagents for municipal and industrial compliance; Product Quality & Innovation (~40% of revenue; Videojet, Linx, Esko, Pantone) provides mission-critical date coding, marking, and packaging workflow solutions. Over 60% of total revenue is recurring consumables and services. Razor-and-blade model creates massive switching costs: testing consumables are a negligible fraction of plant operating costs (<1%) but non-compliance triggers legal shutdown or heavy fines. Owner FCF conversion averages >96% of net income with minimal capex (~1.1% of revenue). Balance sheet is a net cash fortress ($2.03B cash vs $1.97B debt at FY2025; interest coverage 13.3x), allowing disciplined self-funded bolt-on acquisitions and opportunistic share repurchases under the Veralto Enterprise System (VES).
